title: Here to help: customer service
subtitle: prompt, obliging, shoddy, on hold, secure site
summary: Describe good and bad customer service precisely - impeccable or shoddy, responsive or uncooperative - and handle the language of online accounts, dispatch and guarantees.

lesson.heading: Good service
lesson.text: A good company makes sure you get a **prompt** (quick, without delay) reply to any **query**, a question or enquiry, and is very **responsive to** complaints - it listens, takes things seriously and acts. Staff who are **accommodating** are willing to understand and help.

examples.text: I was expecting a **prompt** reply to my email, but I have been waiting two weeks.
When I rang to change the delivery date, they were very **accommodating**.
If you have any **queries** about the service, there is a helpline you can ring.

lesson.heading: Getting back to you
lesson.text: If a company **gets back to you**, it calls or writes with an answer. **Impeccable** service is 100% perfect, and staff who are **obliging** are willing and happy to do things for you.

examples.text: They **got back to** me within ten minutes with a new date.
Whenever I ring, I get **impeccable** service.
Staff in that shop are so **obliging**; they are genuinely helpful.

lesson.heading: Adjectives for bad service
rows: incompetent
failing through insufficient skill, knowledge or training
It wasn't just bad service; they were completely incompetent.
impersonal
lacking a personal element or feeling of human warmth
I find some big shops so impersonal.
shoddy
poor quality (of service or of goods)
They repaired my car but the work was very shoddy.
substandard
below the standard expected (often used about actions)
It was a substandard performance altogether for such a big company.
uncooperative
not supportive, unwilling to work together
The secretary was very uncooperative, so I ended up doing it myself.

lesson.heading: Waiting, complaining and guarantees
lesson.text: A **backlog** is the number of orders waiting to be dealt with. Companies with no **sense of urgency** - no feeling that your request is important - are **exasperating**. You ring the **helpline**, the number where you get help, and they **put you on hold**, that is make you wait. A product that is still **under guarantee** or **under warranty** is covered by a written promise to repair or replace it.

examples.text: There is a huge **backlog** of orders and they can't deliver for three weeks.
They never seem to have any **sense of urgency** when you ring them. It's **exasperating**.
I rang to complain and they **put me on hold** for about 15 minutes.
The home button stopped working but it was still **under guarantee**, so I didn't have to pay.

lesson.heading: Accounts and security online
lesson.text: Most big companies offer a **secure site**, a web address where no outside person can read your details, and where you can **set up an account**. Their **privacy policy** is the set of rules that keeps your account private and guarantees **secure transactions**.

examples.text: Most online stores ask you to **set up an account** before you can buy things.
It's a **secure site** which protects all your personal details.
It didn't feel like a **secure transaction**, so I cancelled it and logged off.

lesson.heading: Links you find on a website
rows: Track your order
follow the progress of your order
Returns policy
rules for sending back goods you are not satisfied with
FAQ
the most commonly asked questions (said as initials)
Check availability
see if the goods you want can be supplied
Browse our categories
look through the range before buying
Site map / site index
with one look you can see what the website contains
Your basket
goods you have chosen but not yet paid for
Privacy and cookies
rules for protecting your personal details and tracking software

lesson.heading: Delivery and shopping in person
lesson.text: Large online stores offer immediate **dispatch** - the goods will be sent at once - and a **nationwide** service, covering the whole country. The **home page** is the main or first page of a website. If you buy something **in-store**, you buy it in a real shop rather than online.

examples.text: They promised immediate **dispatch** of the goods I ordered.
I would recommend you buy your guitar **in-store** rather than online.

lesson.text: Guarantee and warranty mean the same thing here, but we say a product is under guarantee or under warranty - never ~~in guarantee~~.

exercises.prompt: Match each website link with what it does.

pairs.right: follow the progress of your order
see if the goods can be supplied
goods chosen but not yet paid for
see at one look what the website contains
look through the range before buying

exercises.prompt: I rang to complain and they put me ___ for about 15 minutes.
exercises.explanation: To put someone on hold is to make them wait on the telephone.

exercises.prompt: They promised to ring me again, but they never got ___ me.
exercises.explanation: To get back to someone is to call or write with an answer.

exercises.prompt: They promised immediate ___ of the goods I ordered, but nothing has arrived.
exercises.explanation: Dispatch is the sending out of goods.

exercises.prompt: I have always found the company very ___ to complaints and enquiries.
exercises.explanation: To be responsive to something is to listen, take it seriously and act.

exercises.prompt: They said there was a ___ of orders which had built up over the New Year's holiday.
exercises.explanation: A backlog is the number of orders which are waiting to be dealt with.

exercises.prompt: I think you need to try a musical instrument before you buy it, so buy your guitar ___ rather than online.
exercises.explanation: In-store means in a real shop, as opposed to online.

exercises.prompt: Most online stores ask you to ___ an account before you can buy things.
exercises.hint: (enter all the necessary details to open it)
exercises.explanation: To set up an account is to enter all the details necessary to open it.

exercises.prompt: The plumber we got lacked the necessary skills and he caused a flood in our kitchen. He was completely ___.
exercises.explanation: Incompetent means failing through insufficient skill, knowledge or training.

exercises.prompt: The service has no feeling of human warmth about it; they just treat you as a number. The service is very ___.
exercises.explanation: Impersonal service lacks a personal element or feeling of human warmth.

exercises.prompt: The service they gave me could not have been better. It was ___.

exercises.statement: If goods are of poor quality, we can describe them as shoddy.
exercises.explanation: Correct - shoddy describes poor-quality service or goods: the work on my car was very shoddy.

exercises.statement: The new TV came with a two-year promise to repair or replace it, so we say it came with a two-year backlog.
exercises.explanation: The new TV came with a two-year guarantee / warranty. A backlog is orders waiting to be dealt with.

exercises.prompt: Does each word describe good service or bad service?

exercises.answer: They never seem to have any sense of urgency when you ring
exercises.explanation: A sense of urgency is the feeling that your request is important or urgent.
